title: Bringing Ellington and Cab Calloway to San Antonio
summary: Through cousin Barney Bigard, Albert hosted Ellington and Cab in San Antonio and helped book them.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: What about Duke Ellington? You know him personally?

Well sure. Duke and I are great friends. How'd that happen? Well, through Bonnie. Through Bonnie Biggore, my cousin. When they booked the tour in Texas, I wired Bonnie that I was there and I wanted them to be my guests at my house. So I met them in Austin, Texas, which is 75 miles from San Antonio and then I brought them into San Antonio. By the same token, cab the same way. In those days they had what they called the circuit where they played all of these theater dates. That's most of the dates that Ellington and Cab were playing. And then Touloui came to San Antonio if I remember when. Well, it was 1928, 27, 28. And I was responsible for these bookers getting them down there.
When did they have that flood there?
No, in the 20s. Wasn't that a big flood? No. Not that I remember.
Yeah, it might have been before you got there. Might have been before, but there was a bad flood here a few years ago in the 50s. It almost washed my nightclub away.
But what about those band leaders when they came then, the musicians? Did they have trouble finding a place to stay? Well, sure they did.
